prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Asset type: a full printed plate for the ReEnchanted Book's November 2026 issue, The Guest Who Came on All Souls, printed in a 6 by 9 inch book on uncoated book paper inside a white mat and a thin gold rule. Input images are STYLE AND CHARACTER REFERENCES ONLY: match their exquisite hand-drawn ink-and-watercolour storybook rendering, irregular fine brown pen contours, fine crosshatching, dense lovingly observed material detail, warm muted washes on cream paper. November's palette: lamplight amber, copper, oatmeal and flour white, bread-crust browns, holly green, and a cold frost blue that only appears near the west door and after dark. An old illustrated faerie book, physical and a little feral, warm but with something wrong at the edge of it, never childish. A full painted scene with its own background whose edges soften into cream paper in a gentle vignette. No border, no frame, no lettering, no legible words, no labels, no captions, no watermark, no speech bubbles; any writing in the scene is illegible pen scribble. Print-safe colour for uncoated paper: no pure black, no neon, no large flat dark areas; keep shadows open and textured. Characters must match their reference portraits exactly in face, hair and clothing, drawn as real people with weight and warmth, never caricatures. The reader of the Book is never shown; at most an anonymous hand at the edge of the picture holding an old leather-bound book. Avoid flat vector art, clipart, glossy 3D, photorealism, anime, gore and modern objects.
Composition: landscape, 3:2.
Subject: Supper at the long table in the Kitchens: every plate in the building, odd and good, candles stuck in saucers down the middle, soup, ham, a well of mashed potato, cranberry sauce cut with a knife. At the head of the table one empty chair with a full plate, a candle and a napkin folded into a little hat. The small hooded figure eats on a bench halfway down, looking almost at home.
Present: Ambrose Trencher (big older cook, grey beard, cap, stained canvas apron, sleeves rolled); Penny Blackletter (young woman, dark curls pinned up, round spectacles, dark waistcoat over a white blouse with a cravat, ink on her fingers; match her reference portrait exactly); Serenity Brown (young woman, long wild dark curls, sea-green coat, a brass compass on a chain; moves slightly sideways, always half-seeing something beyond); The Guest: a small figure, about elbow-height to a grown man, in a long green coat far too big for it with tarnished brass buttons and a ragged hem, sleeves rolled up four times, the hood always up so no face shows, only two very clean small hands; it should feel old, polite and faintly uncanny, never cute and never a monster.
Production request: native 2400x1600 pixels if supported. ONE continuous full supper scene; no collage, notes, annotation, border, inset or copied lettering. Image1 is painting-style reference only; do not include goblin or cat. Images2–5 identify Ambrose, Penny, Serenity and Guest respectively. All four distinct faces/clothing identities preserved; Guest's hood entirely hides its face. Clearly show unoccupied head chair with its full plate, candle and napkin hat; Guest is seated halfway along bench, not in empty chair.
review: Second attempt visually inspected: reserved place now clearly has full supper plate with ham, mashed potato and cranberry serving; intact napkin hat moved immediately beside plate; empty tall chair and candle retained. All cast identities and surrounding scene retained.

editPrompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Change ONLY the reserved place setting at the empty tall wooden head chair on the RIGHT of this exact supper illustration. This place must visibly be set with a FULL PLATE of supper: clear slices of ham, a mound of mashed potato and a portion of red cranberry sauce on an individual blue-and-white plate directly in front of that empty chair. The folded white linen napkin hat currently fills that empty plate: move the intact little napkin hat a few centimetres onto the table immediately beside the full plate so both hat and generous food serving are clearly visible. Keep its candle, the empty tall chair and its position unchanged. Preserve absolutely everything else: all four characters' exact faces, hair, skin tones, hands, clothing, poses and locations; the Guest hood remains entirely faceless; every bowl, serving dish, room detail, light, pen-and-watercolour rendering, cream vignette and composition. Only add the full supper plate and move that one napkin hat beside it. No text, no collage, no additional people.
